9-1-1 est une série dramatique qui plong: 9-1-1 is a dramatic series that plunges into the heart of the crises that hit American citizens and highlights the heroic work of first responders. Through stories from police, firefighters and ambulances, the series offers us a perspective on the challenges they face on a daily basis. Each episode reminds us of the crucial importance of the 9-1-1 emergency number, which is a true link between those in distress and those who work for their safety. The heroes of this series are embodied in a casting composed of Angela Bassett in the role of Athena Grant, a determined and competent police officer, and Peter Krause in the role of Bobby Nash, the fire chief. Together, they lead a diverse team of stakeholders, each bringing their unique skills and personal stories. Jennifer Love Hewitt also joins the casting as a 9-1-1 operator, who has to navigate in stressful situations while facing her own emotional struggles. At each episode, viewers witness moments of extreme tension, whether in dangerous interventions, tragic accidents or personal crises. The series deals with real social issues, such as domestic violence, natural disasters and even unlikely catastrophic situations, while exploring how these events affect not only victims but also the actors themselves. Between moments of bravery and vulnerability, 9 -1-1 reminds us that behind every call to 9-1-1 is a human history, full of courage, sacrifice and hope. Thus, this series invites the public to reflect on the essential role these heroes play in our lives. 9-1-1 is not only a series of emergency interventions, but also an exploration of human ties in times of crisis, while paying tribute to those who risk their lives to save others' lives.

Entre la Dent de Géant, le mythique Cerv: Between the Giant Dent, the mythical Matterhorn and the dreadful northern face of the Eiger, three giants who haunt the dreams of the climbers, two friends are preparing to face their demons as well as the elements. Michael (Freddie Thorp), a former tragically-marked climbing enthusiast, turned his back on the mountain after his sister disappeared in an accident. But today, alongside his childhood friend JP (Michel Biel), he tries to overcome his fears to fulfill this long-refused dream. Their journey begins in Chamonix, where they join a group of young, daring mountaineers. If their energy is communicative, their carelessness and their taste for risk are quickly worrying Michael, whose instinct of prudence sages at every climbing meter. The first two ascents, the Dent de Géant and the Matterhorn, confirm his fears: unforeseen cracks, precipitated decisions, underestimated equipment... Tensions are rising in the group, between those who see the mountain as a playground and those who respect the danger. But it is on the ice slopes of the Eiger, nicknamed "the Wall", that the expedition is tilting. A storm of unprecedented violence is taking hold on them, turning their last challenge into a desperate struggle for survival. Cut off from the world by screaming gusts and blinding snow, rescues become an illusion. Now every decision, every movement, can seal their fate. Between the vertical walls of the adrenaline and the introspection of the nights in tent, where ghosts of the past reappear, Summit Fever explores the limits of friendship, trust and resilience. How far will they go to go to go down alive? And at what cost? Will the mountain, indifferent and sublime, give them a final lesson, or will it become their tomb?

Au cœur de Manhattan, là où les gratte-c: In the heart of Manhattan, where skyscrapers hide as many dreams as nightmares, an elite criminal police unit is fighting relentlessly against one of the darkest scourges in society: sexual crimes. Under the inflexible but caring leadership of Captain Don Cragen (Dann Florek), this specialized team combines professional rigour and human commitment, placing victim protection at the centre of every investigation. In a world where violence leaves invisible traces, these police officers must not only track down the perpetrators, but also restore the dignity of those who have been broken. Among them, Inspectors Olivia Benson (Mariska Hargitay) and Elliot Stabler (Christopher Meloni) form an emblematic duo, united by unwavering determination and empathy that pushes them to invest far beyond the files. Benson, whose personal past has created a strong sensitivity to the suffering of victims, especially women and children, embodies a calm force in the face of horror. Stabler, a passionate family member, brings combative energy, sometimes at the limit of obsession, to bring justice to the fore. Together, they navigate through the meandering of the most icy cases, where every detail counts and where each testimony can cause an investigation to tip over. Over time, the unit evolves with the arrival of new members. Each case confronts them with a heartbreaking reality: broken lives, silences that are complicit, and systems that too often fail to protect the most vulnerable. Between the interview rooms where tight parts are played, the streets of New York where every shadow can conceal a danger, and the personal lives of these policemen – marked by the emotional repercussions of their profession – the series explores without fail the complexities of justice and redemption. Here, victories are measured as much as the convictions obtained as the lives saved, and each episode reminds that behind the statistics are destinies hidden. 10 septembre 2012. Trois coups de feu re: 10 September 2012. Three shots were fired at a house in the Creuse. Norbert Marot, a 72-year-old man, collapses, fatally hit in the back. Behind the weapon, his wife, Jacqueline Sauvage (Muriel Robin), 65, after 47 years of marriage. This brutal gesture ended decades of silence, but opened one of the most cleavage trials of the decade. For behind this murder is a much darker story: that of a woman who claims to have suffered domestic violence, rape and kidnapping for almost half a century, in general indifference. Before the judges, Jacqueline described a domestic hell – a tyrannical, alcoholic husband who had no reason to beat his daughters, humiliated them and treated them as slaves. Children, now adults, confirm his words: they grew up in terror, powerless witnesses of beatings and abuse. Yet when the verdict falls, it is the astounding: sentenced to 10 years in prison, Jacqueline is convicted, without the mitigating circumstances sufficient to exonerate her.
